page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9a.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 9T25 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. Operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz, the server delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

The instance configuration does not include local storage disks or hardware GPU acceleration, mandating external network-attached volumes for persistent data storage. Networking capabilities are anchored by a 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, accommodating large data transfers across cloud resources, though complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provided.

With its balanced allocation of compute and memory resources along with dedicated CPU pinning, the instance eliminates multi-tenant resource contention. It is suited for workloads requiring reliable multi-threaded CPU and memory density, such as enterprise application servers, mid-to-large transactional databases, distributed caching layers, and containerized CI/CD build environments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9a.16xlarge is a balanced general-purpose virtual server configured with 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs running on an AMD EPYC 9T25 processor at 2.7 GHz. Accompanied by 256 GB of system memory, the instance maintains a consistent 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation, supporting steady multi-threaded execution without noisy-neighbor contention. The system omits dedicated GPUs and contains no bundled local disk storage, relying entirely on network-attached block storage for system and application data. High-throughput data communication is facilitated by a 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, although no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. This hardware architecture provides predictable resource density for enterprise-grade workloads, including high-concurrency web application backends, container orchestrators, relational databases, data transformation pipelines, and distributed software build clusters requiring substantial CPU core counts alongside proportional RAM.
